title: Streaming-rate lab harness for tokens/sec and p95 regression detection
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Build a robust lab harness that simulates realistic client streaming behaviors and measures tokens/sec (TPS), p95 latency, and regression signals for our core serving models. The harness must support cold vs warm KV cache modes, variable sequence lengths, bursty microbursts and sustained flows, and produce stable metrics suitable for CI gating, nightly baselines, and long-term trend dashboards. Outputs should include per-run artifacts (raw samples, aggregated stats, histograms, and GPU occupancy traces) and a deterministic pipeline for automated regression detection and bisecting.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can run canonical scenarios (short prompt burst, long prompt steady, mixed workload) against a selected model and produce reproducible TPS and p95 metrics
CI nightly job is configured and uploads artifacts to perfbench S3 path with run metadata and raw traces
Regression detector flags anomalies using EWMA + CUSUM rules and posts a Slack summary with links to artifacts when threshold crossed
A simple auto-bisect workflow is documented and exercised end-to-end for at least one historical regression (link provided)
Dashboard tile added to Console perf workspace showing rolling 30-day TPS and p95 baselines with annotated CI runs

progress_updates: 2025-11-11: Kickoff meeting — agreed canonical scenarios and metrics; Rafael to prototype simulator; Aisha to define seed corpus

Next: finalize alert thresholds, add auto-bisect hook, and run a controlled regression reproduction to validate detector sensitivity
notes: Implementation notes: sample at 50Hz token-emission granularity for streaming; record per-token timestamps to compute instantaneous TPS distribution; compute p95 using block bootstrap to quantify variance; use GPU occupancy + kernel trace to correlate TPS regressions with kernel selection changes. For CI gating, use a two-stage policy: alert (soft) for 3-night drift, block PRs when single-run p95 degradation >15% AND TPS drop >10% with statistical significance (p<0.05).
